<!--
  algorithm — domain-specific computation or algorithm definition. Records how a metric, index, or
  score is derived; the source of truth for computation semantics when the product defines its own
  calculation.
  Lives at: `product/algorithms/<kebab-name>.md`.
  Authorship: canonical. SLO: 180d, AND stale whenever any page `realizes:` names is updated after this one —
    either trigger fires. The timer stays alongside the edge: the rule as implemented can drift even though the
    feature it realizes has not changed.
  Owner: fixed to `product`, do not substitute.
  Distinct from: a feature (the user-facing capability — link it via related:); a concept (the mental
    model — link it via related: or domain-concept:).
  Variants: Formula shape — a single-index metric with a defined algorithm; Narrative shape — a hub,
    pipeline, or reconciliation metric with no single formula. The shape guides how `## Algorithm`
    reads; it does not change the section set.
  Columns: Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Extra frontmatter: `realizes` is REQUIRED — the feature(s) or module this page realizes; a page
    that serves the system generally rather than one module realizes `[[product:app-base]]`
    instead (see [[_authoring:wiki-page-types]]). `domain-concept: [[domain:concepts/<slug>]]` is OPTIONAL — set
    when an industry-standard equivalent concept exists; omit the frontmatter line when none applies.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}}.
-->

## Definition
<!-- What this methodology computes, in plain language. One paragraph.
     Use user-facing and domain terms, not implementation vocabulary. Open with the page's lead sentence — see [[_authoring:wiki-authoring-spec#lead-sentence]]. -->

## Inputs
<!-- The values, signals, or entities consumed by the algorithm.
     One bullet per input. Reference entities via [[entities/<module>/<name>]] where they exist. -->

## Parameters
<!-- Every tunable constant the algorithm depends on, one row each: its value, where
     that value came from, and how well grounded it is. A constant with no stated source
     is a magic number, and a reader cannot tell a measured threshold from a guess.

     | Parameter | Value | Source | Grounding |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | `<name>` | `<value>` | <where it came from> | estimated / grounded / calibrated |

     *estimated* — chosen by judgment, not yet checked against data. *grounded* — derived
     from a measurement or an external standard, named in Source. *calibrated* — tuned
     against this system's own data, with the tuning run named.

     "None." when the algorithm has no tunables. This section absorbs what pages
     otherwise spread across "Starting values", "Parameters" and "Calibration status" —
     one concern, one home. -->

## Algorithm
<!-- The computation steps or formula. Use a numbered list or
     code block for step-by-step derivation. Keep language-neutral — this is
     product intent, not implementation. A Narrative-shape metric has no single formula: describe the
     pipeline or reconciliation here, or point at the sibling pages that compute the parts. -->

## Output
<!-- What the methodology produces: the metric value, score, or result.
     Include units, value range, and interpretation notes (e.g. "higher is better"). -->

## vs. industry baseline
<!-- How this methodology differs from or aligns with the linked industry-standard concept.
     One to two paragraphs. If the two are currently identical, note that explicitly
     so readers know the comparison was made. With no `domain-concept` set, write "None." -->
